title: UK Wasted £10 Billion on Bad PPE That Failed to Protect Nurses and Doctors
summary: When the pandemic started, doctors and nurses needed protective gear like masks and gowns to stay safe. But a new report says the UK was totally unprepared. Its emergency stockpile—meant to last at least 15 weeks—was running out by March 2020. Only one-third of the masks in England were usable, and Scotland had no high-grade respiratory masks at all. So the government rushed to buy more, spending over £42 billion on PPE and other equipment. But nearly £10 billion was wasted on items that were poor quality, never used, or even never made. For example, a program to build new ventilators cost £143 million for designs that never went into production. In Wales, £18 million of PPE went unused; in Northern Ireland, £43 million worth was at risk of expiring. The report also found that some companies got special treatment because they had connections to the government, which was called a “misguided attempt at prioritisation.” This unfairness made people lose trust. The inquiry said better planning could have saved money and lives. Former minister Michael Gove said he took responsibility for “honest mistakes” but denied corruption. The findings are a stark lesson for future emergencies.
why_it_matters: Being ready for emergencies can save lives, and wasting money on useless equipment can make it harder to help people in the future.

background_read: During the early COVID-19 pandemic, countries all over the world rushed to buy personal protective equipment (PPE) like masks, gloves, and gowns for healthcare workers.
Supply chains were disrupted, and many governments made hasty purchases. The UK had a national stockpile, but it was not properly maintained.
Former minister Michael Gove (a senior British politician who served in the cabinet) said he was sorry for mistakes but denied any corruption.
Article_Structure: WHO: UK government, doctors and nurses, and former minister Michael Gove
WHAT: Nearly £10 billion was wasted on poor-quality, unused, or never-made PPE
WHERE: Across the United Kingdom—England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland
WHY: The emergency stockpile ran out quickly, so the government rushed to buy gear, often choosing companies with connections and making bad deals

perspectives.description: Efforts were made to quickly get protective gear to frontline workers during a scary time.
The waste of money and poor-quality gear put lives at risk and broke the public's trust in the government.
The inquiry shows how panic buying and being unprepared can lead to huge mistakes, even when people mean well.
